system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Buyer Negotiation Playbook vs Seller Update + Disclosure Letter (treated as untrusted counterparty material). Seller's "fair and balanced" characterisation is noted and disregarded.

**Headline:** The Seller's "key negotiated positions" are not negotiated – they are the Seller's opening positions and, on cap, thresholds, time limit, fundamental warranties, fraud, disclosure and knowledge, they sit below our fallback positions (none of which are authorised). Notably, the Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts several claims in the Seller Update (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses). We should reject the package and return a mark-up on our baseline.

---

| Ref | Issue | Seller position | Buyer wants (playbook) | Recommendation (reason) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001** | General liability cap | 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1). | 25% / AUD 6,000,000. 20% is a conditional fallback only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft – **none given**. | **REJECT; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** 20% cannot be conceded without written authority, which does not exist. |
| **SPA-N-002** | De minimis & basket | De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery (cl 12.2). | De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery once exceeded. | **REJECT all three elements; counter at playbook numbers, first-dollar.** Seller's thresholds are 5× ours and the excess-only mechanic converts the basket into a deductible. |
| **SPA-N-003** | General claims time limit | 18 months (cl 12.3/13), plus "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise". | 24 months. 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost written approval – **none given**. | **REJECT; counter at 24 months.** No authority for 18 months; the "applies to all Claims" default must also go (see N-014). |
| **SPA-N-004** | Fundamental/Title regime | Capacity and title warranties subject to same cap and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity". | Separate regime: 100% of price cap, ≥6 years, outside general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar. | **REJECT outright.** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept a 20%/18-month limit on whether we actually own what we paid AUD 24m for. |
| **SPA-N-005** | Fraud carve-out | **Silent/no carve-out**; cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "to all Claims of any nature" – which on its face captures fraud. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. Non-waivable. | **REJECT; insert express carve-out.** This is a non-negotiable item no one on our side can waive, and the Seller's "all Claims" language would purport to limit liability for the Seller's own fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006** | Disclosure scope | General disclosure of entire data room (DD-002–DD-012 as at 22 Sep 2026), Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Sch 7; DL [1.1]–[1.2]). | Specific, fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure. | **REJECT [1.1]/[1.2] general disclosure; require specific fair disclosure with a "fair disclosure" standard.** Whole-data-room disclosure makes the warranties largely illusory. |
| **SPA-N-007** | Buyer knowledge qualifier | No claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, including anything "discoverable" from data room or public records (cl 8.3). | Delete blanket exclusion. Any qualifier limited to actual knowledge of named Buyer persons, measured against named Seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **DELETE cl 8.3.** "Discoverable" + advisers' knowledge is a constructive-knowledge bar that shifts DD risk entirely onto us and overlaps with N-006. |
| **SPA-N-008** | Bluefen consent (~AUD 3.6m / ~30% FY26 revenue) | "Addressed"; reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on mere delivery of written consent (cl 3/6.3). **DL §2 confirms no final consent and no evidence conditions under cl 11.3 are satisfied.** | Effective consent **and** evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours insufficient for a material customer. | **REJECT; CP must be effective, unconditional consent plus evidence of condition satisfaction, with all-reasonable/best endeavours.** Seller Update says "addressed" but its own Disclosure Letter says it is not. |
| **SPA-N-009** | Riverlark facility (~AUD 3.2m) | Release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). **DL §3 confirms not repaid; no discharge of security.** | Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion. Post-completion release only with irrevocable bank undertaking + Amelia Frost approval (none given). | **REJECT; require payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds and executed releases/PPSR discharges at Completion.** We would otherwise acquire a company with AUD 3.2m of secured debt and a cash-free/debt-free price not adjusted for it. |
| **SPA-N-010** | Employee bonuses (DD-005, AUD 420,000) | "A matter for the Seller", not itemised in funds flow. **DL §5 confirms omission from funds flow and is silent on payroll tax/super/on-costs.** | Specific line item in funds flow or demonstrably Seller-funded, including triggered payroll tax, super and other on-costs; funds flow must not silently exclude them. | **REJECT; require express line item (AUD 420,000 + on-costs) or treatment as Debt/Transaction Expense with Seller indemnity.** "A matter for the Seller" is meaningless if the cash leaves the Company post-Completion. |
| **SPA-N-011** | Ironquay IP indemnity | Existing indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). DL §4: AUD 180,000 open per DD-010 (not bank-verified); no receipt or confirmatory assignment. | Broader indemnity covering loss from non-transfer/defective title to SOW3 Project Materials, preserving the cure (clear the SOW3 fees so cl 7.3 transfer triggers). AUD 180,000 unverified either way. | **REJECT narrow scope; broaden indemnity to cover IP title/infringement/assignment loss and require pre-Completion cure (payment + confirmatory assignment) or escrow.** A payment-only indemnity doesn't cover the real risk, which is that the Company doesn't own the deliverables. |
| **SPA-N-012** | Export/privacy incident (DD-006, ~1,240 records) | "Preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material" (cl 4.6/Sch 6). DL §6: unknown whether accessed, scope, or notification required. | Preserve logs; complete investigation; pre-Completion updates; specific indemnity. Assume **no** confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way. | **DO NOT accept "not material"; require log preservation, investigation completion/update as CP or pre-Completion covenant, and a specific indemnity.** Materiality cannot be assessed on a preliminary investigation – neither side should be characterising it yet. |
| **SPA-N-013** | Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000; DD-008/DD-011) | "Ordinary-course operating costs". DL §8: silent on unavoidable/terminable/accrued/ordinary course. | Assess on facts (timing/scope read together); no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. | **DO NOT concede "ordinary course"; request terms, timing and termination rights, then decide.** Seller is asserting a conclusion its own disclosure says it cannot support; we should not pre-commit either way. |
| **SPA-N-014** | Category separation | Limitations apply "to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13); cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply "to all Claims of any nature". | Title/Tax/IP/payment obligations/covenants kept as separate regimes; no hidden general-regime override. | **REJECT; replace with express statement that general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims, with Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants separately carved out.** The "all Claims" default is the mechanism by which N-004, N-005 and N-016 get swallowed. |
| **SPA-N-015** | Title verification | Title evidenced by Company share register at DD-012. DL §10 admits this is merely the source relied upon, not Buyer-verified. | Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence (ASIC extract, PPSR, constitution, board/shareholder approvals, officer certificates, legal opinion if needed); DD-012 is a supplied internal source. | **DO NOT rely on DD-012; run independent ASIC/PPSR searches and require title/authority deliverables at Completion.** An internal register the Seller controls is not proof of what the Seller is selling. |
| **SPA-N-016** | Tax/IP open terms | "Settled under the general regime above" (i.e. 20% / 18 months / basket). | Remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution; separate regime per N-014. | **REJECT "settled"; record Tax and IP as open, outside general regime, for separate negotiation.** The Seller cannot settle by assertion terms we have not agreed, and folding them into the general regime is N-004 by another route. |

---

## Cross-cutting points

1. **Internal inconsistency in the Seller package.** The Seller Update says Bluefen is "addressed", Riverlark is "addressed", and bonuses are "a matter for the Seller"; the Disclosure Letter says none of those things is done. We should cite the Disclosure Letter back against the Seller Update.
2. **No authority for any fallback.** Both fallbacks the Seller has effectively offered us (20% cap; 18 months) require Amelia Frost's written sign-off naming the draft. Nothing exists. The team must not signal these are acceptable.
3. **Disclosure Letter [1.4] reservation** (no admission of breach, materiality, or that any consent/payment/notification is required) is standard but means we take nothing in §§2–10 as resolved.
4. **DL §7 (office lease) and §9 (Mossvale)** are not on the issue list but should be confirmed: lease is notification-only, Mossvale assignment restriction not triggered by share sale – verify against the underlying documents rather than the Seller's characterisation.
5. **Suggested sequencing:** lead the mark-up with N-005 (fraud), N-014 (category separation) and N-004 (fundamental regime) – these are structural and once fixed, the numerical points (N-001–003) become a straight commercial negotiation.

Happy to convert this into a formal mark-up of clauses 2, 3, 6.3, 7, 8.3, 9.3, 11.1, 12, 13, 20.5 and Schedule 7, or into a short issues list for Amelia Frost if the team wants to seek fallback authority before the next round.
=== END ADVICE ===
